clue.text: Big blows

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means huge or very large

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an informal adjective for enormous, and a noun for a series of hard hits.

clue.text: Constrain worker to go on strike

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Restraining a worker who wants to go on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff is to restrain or shackle, used figuratively for limiting freedom.

clue.text: Complete discretion to distribute the small credit balance

indicators.note: to distribute means spreading the letters out into a new order

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit

explanation.surface: Being given free rein to share out the remaining small credit balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche is full freedom to act as one wishes, literally a blank card.

clue.text: Exempt from death culprit finally caught in wrong

indicators.note: caught in means the letter is trapped inside the word for wrong

parts.note: immoral means morally wrong

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of culprit

explanation.surface: A culprit escapes execution after being caught in wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortal means not subject to dying, living for ever.

clue.text: Measure — state to express an opinion about half of it

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: about means the vote goes around the half letter

parts.note: to vote is to express an opinion

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word it is its last letter

explanation.surface: A state invited to give its view on half of some measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old word for a dance, and the gavotte is a French dance.

clue.text: Tailless worm inside strange tree

indicators.note: inside places the shortened worm within the word for strange

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or odd

indicators.note: tailless removes the final letter of the word for worm

parts.note: to worm one's way is to edge along

explanation.surface: A worm with no tail found inside a peculiar tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' cuts EDGE to EDG, which goes into RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Red gum is a eucalyptus of Australia, named for its red resin.

clue.text: Fish with a tailpiece

parts.note: cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish served with a piece of its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music, its concluding section.

clue.text: You can chew it, as schoolboy said to Head

indicators.note: said means the schoolboy's name is spoken to give the first part

parts.note: Beetle is a schoolboy in Kipling's school stories Stalky and Co
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A schoolboy talking to the headmaster about something to chew.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is one of the three boys in Rudyard Kipling's Stalky & Co, schoolboy tales; his name sounds like BETEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca seed is wrapped in leaves and chewed as a mild stimulant across South Asia.

clue.text: Story troubling noted ace

indicators.note: troubling the words disturbs them, so their letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A tale that upsets a celebrated top performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting tale told in conversation.

clue.text: This sticks out of trunk, but goes back in it

definitions.text: This sticks out of trunk, but goes back in it

indicators.note: goes back tells us the run of letters found is read from right to left
in says the letters sit within the single word trunk

explanation.surface: A riddle about something protruding from a tree trunk that also lies hidden within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds RUNK inside 'trunk'; 'goes back' turns it round. The whole clue also describes a knot growing out of a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A knur is a knot or hard lump on a tree trunk, a protruding growth.

clue.text: Full board — that's the way

parts.note: thorough means complete or full
board in the sense of meals provided is fare

explanation.surface: Someone praising a hotel's full board arrangement as the right way to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public route through a place.

clue.text: Unavoidable mishap damaged carefree jumbo: leaving Brazil's capital

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of carefree jumbo are broken up and rearranged
capital means the first letter of Brazil

explanation.surface: An elephant with no worries hurt in an accident as it leaves the Brazilian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' says the B (Brazil's capital) goes out of CAREFREEJUMBO before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Force majeure is an irresistible event such as a disaster that excuses a party from a contract.

clue.text: About to dry fish

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the whole sequence of pieces round

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone about to dry a fish after catching it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns TO plus BRUT (dry, of champagne) backwards as one run: TOBRUT read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbot is a large flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: Schoolboy right to confess following one of 22

indicators.note: following says the next pieces come after the burial place

parts.note: the answer at 22 across is a plural word for burial places, and one such place is a tomb
to own up is to confess, so own means confess

explanation.surface: A schoolboy who has the right to confess after one of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown is the hero of Thomas Hughes's Victorian novel Tom Brown's School Days, set at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional pupil of Rugby School is the most famous literary schoolboy in English.

clue.text: Friendly fellow featured in a fiction

indicators.note: featured in puts the fellow's letter inside the phrase a fiction

parts.note: a fable is a made-up story, a fiction

explanation.surface: A pleasant character who appears in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means good-natured and easy to talk to, warmly sociable.

clue.text: In an emergency, a military force lands quietly on island

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: In a crisis, an army unit makes a silent landing on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch means if really necessary, when pushed by circumstances.

clue.text: Bats are swung, side by side

indicators.note: swung suggests the letters are swung about into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Two batsmen swinging their bats together at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means level with each other, in a line facing the same way.

clue.text: One starting to ask for a ring

parts.note: to beg is to ask for something
an inner is the ring next to the bull on a target

explanation.surface: A novice asking for a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone just starting out at something.

clue.text: Hypnotist leaving in confusion after termination of hypnosis

indicators.note: after says the scrambled letters follow the last letter of hypnosis
termination of means the final letter of hypnosis
in confusion means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hypnotist leaving in a muddle when a hypnosis session ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Svengali, the mesmerist of du Maurier's Trilby, fits a clue whose surface pretends to be about a hypnotist walking off flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the sinister mesmerist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, now a byword for a controlling manipulator.

clue.text: Shilling off noisy rocket

indicators.note: off means the shilling letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: strident means loud and harsh
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: A shilling taken off a loud firework.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is a submarine-launched ballistic missile used by Britain and the USA.

clue.text: Go ahead, no fences down

definitions.meaning: a signal that it is safe to proceed
in show jumping, a round with no obstacles knocked over is clear for every fence

explanation.definitionFit: A permission signal to proceed, and a show-jumping round where every obstacle is cleared.

clue.text: Movable sight-screen?

parts.note: a cricket sight-screen helps batsmen see; here the screen shields the sight of the eye and can be raised and lowered

explanation.surface: A cricket sight-screen that can be wheeled about.
explanation.walkthrough: A sight-screen is a large white board behind the bowler at cricket grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin closes over the eye, a screen for vision that moves.

clue.text: Chases wine

definitions.meaning: to chase metal is to engrave it, and to grave is an old word for engrave
a wine region near Bordeaux and its red and white wines

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for carving or engraving, and a Bordeaux district famous for its wine.

clue.text: Enough to live on in Missouri :

definitions.meaning: having enough money to live on means not relying on anyone else
a city in the US state of Missouri

explanation.definitionFit: Financial self-sufficiency, and a city near Kansas City in Missouri.

clue.text: Bird plunged into the water

definitions.meaning: a pigeon-like bird, symbol of peace
the past tense of dive, used in North America and dialect

explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon-family bird, and the past tense of the verb to dive.

clue.text: Part of America, part without a harbour

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the words without a harbour is taken

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the USA that has no harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a landlocked state in the western United States.

clue.text: Not serving well-mannered Scot

parts.note: civil means polite or well-mannered
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A polite Scotsman who is not in the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian is someone not serving in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Retired chap in the City

indicators.note: in places the chap's name within the name of the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
Ned is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man who has retired from work in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial district, but here it is just a city, Turin.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is to go to bed, which is also what retiring means.
